stories.title: Israel-Backed Palestinian Militias Terrorize Displaced Families in Gaza
stories.text: Youssef Al-Sheikh in his home in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza describes a raid by an Israel-backed Palestinian militia last month. JABALIYA REFUGEE CAMP, Gaza Strip—Youssef Al-Sheikh was asleep with his wife and eight young children in a room on the ground floor of a badly damaged building in the wasteland of northern Gaza’s Jabaliya refugee camp when the group of masked, heavily armed members of an Israeli-backed Palestinian militia broke down the door and stormed inside. It was around 2 a.m. on the night of September 24. Decked out in tactical gear and with their assault rifles pointing menacingly down at his family, they began shouting at Al-Sheikh to get up. The light from their military headlamps pierced the darkness, blinding Al-Sheikh. “They came inside, and as soon as they entered, one of them raised his Kalashnikov and aimed it at me while I was here,” Al-Sheikh told Drop Site News, pointing to the only bed in the room, made up of thin mattress laid on a thin piece of wood propped up on concrete blocks. “About seven people came in. stories.title: AI Industry Leader Wants 50 Free Kills
stories.text: This is a web version of The Lever ’s daily email newsletter. The artificial intelligence firm Anthropic has pitched itself as a pro-regulation, “ safety-first ” alternative to its competitors — but sample rules quietly circulating on Capitol Hill reveal the staggering scale of what the firm is willing to sacrifice for AI dominance. The draft legislation, proposed by Anthropic and obtained by Politico , would let the federal government interfere with an AI model’s release only if it risks immediate, predictable damages of more than $1 billion or 50 human deaths… potentially giving AI firms dozens of free kills. Anthropic’s draft bill also requires AI developers to submit a variety of security and safety data to the federal government, while simultaneously creating an exemption blocking these records from Freedom of Information Act requests. These terms closely mirror those in an Anthropic-endorsed California state law signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) — roughly a year after he vetoed a much stronger AI safety bill . stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: Meta shuts down "No Kings" account during major anti-Trump protest
stories.text: It was a critical day for the anti-Trump protest group, which has attracted millions of participants since 2025. Saturday’s events focused on early voter activation ahead of the midterm elections. Then, at around 1:30 p.m. Eastern, No Kings’ Instagram account was taken offline . It left the organization without its biggest megaphone during the height of the protests. The account remained offline for approximately 90 minutes. Even after the account was restored, it took until after 5 p.m. before No Kings could post new content to the account. Common Cause called Meta’s actions “ an alarming act of corporate censorship ,” accusing the company of deplatforming “grassroots voter mobilization efforts.” Just after 6 p.m., Meta spokesperson Andy Stone released a statement , claiming the suspension was an “error”: When accounts post, share or comment at very high frequencies it can trigger automated systems. That’s what happened with the No Kings IG account in the lead up to today’s day of action. Unfortunately, that automated action was clearly taken in error.
